facts.text: Santa Teresa hosts a 1,100‑acre rail park that connects the Santa Teresa Southern Railroad to Union Pacific, making it a key rail interchange.
The town’s roots trace back to a Spanish‑era land grant called the Santa Teresa Grant, whose title was confirmed by U.S. courts between 1895 and 1900.
Developer Charlie Crowder envisioned an industrial zone along the U.S.-Mexico border in 1964, partnering with Mexican President Adolfo López Mateos to spur cross‑border commerce.
By 1970 Crowder secured 1,800 acres from the Santa Teresa Grant and 6,000 acres through a land exchange, forming the community’s eastern core west of McNutt Road.
Livestock imports from Mexico paused in June 2025 due to a New World screwworm outbreak, then resumed on July 21, 2025 under USDA surveillance coordinated with Mexican authorities.
